Q: Did a validation to filter active/inactive cellphone number from database A:

The accepted answer suggests numVerify, but it’s important to distinguish between ‘Valid Syntax’ and ‘Active Status’.

Most validation APIs (including numVerify) only check if the number is valid according to the carrier plan (i.e., it exists). They often do not check if the subscriber is active or if the line is currently connected to the network.

If you need to filter ‘Active/Inactive’ specifically (as asked), you need a lookup that provides actual phone status.

I am part of Trestle, and we built an Phone Validation API specifically for this. It returns a Phone Activity Score (based on real-time network usage) and Line Type Fidelity (distinguishing Mobile vs. VoIP). If you just want to clean a database of dead numbers, checking ‘Activity’ is much more effective than checking ‘Validity’.

Q: How to get first N elements of a list in C#? A:

This is not a Linq solution but since you want a Python-like way, here is the C# Indices and Ranges syntax to get the first two items of an array:

        int[] numbers = { 0, 1, 2, 3 };
        int[] firstTwo = numbers[0..2];

Notes:

  • This requires C# 8 or above.
  • Start of the range is inclusive
  • End of the range is exclusive (Hence we use [0..2] not [0..1])

Q: BizTalk Server 2020: Best practice for exposing HTTP POST endpoint to receive JSON and write to file (HTTP adapter vs WCF-WebHttp) A:

Thanks. I finally got it to work, including HTTPS. I learned a lot along the way.

Here’s what I did:

IIS

  • Created an IIS application using the WCF Service Publishing Wizard with the Service Endpoint option.

  • Enabled anonymous authentication.

  • Created a new application pool where the application pool identity has access to the BizTalk databases.

  • Configured a server certificate and added an HTTPS binding.

BizTalk Administration Console

  • Created a one-way receive port.

  • Configured a WCF-WebHttp receive location.

  • Set Security mode to: Transport
